name: Minutes - August 5, 2024
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  Meeting of the
  City of Huntington Park City Council
  Monday, August 5, 2024

The regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Huntington Park, California was
called to order at 6:03 p.m. on Monday, August 5, 2024, in the Council Chambers at City
Hall, 6550 Miles Avenue, Huntington Park, California; Mayor Karina Macias presiding.

PRESENT: Council Member(s): Esmeralda Castillo, Jonathan Sanabria, Eduardo
“Eddie” Martinez, Vice Mayor Arturo Flores and Mayor Karina Macias

ABSENT:  None

CITY OFFICIALS/STAFF: City Manager Ricardo Reyes; Eduardo Sarmiento City Clerk;
Cosme Lozano Police Chief; Steve Forster Director of Community Development and
Interim Director of Public Works; Sergio Infanzon Director of Communications; Cynthia
Norzagaray Director of Parks and Recreation; Arnold M. Alvarez-Glasman City Attorney.

INVOCATION
Mayor Macias led the invocation.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
Councilmember Sanabria led Pledge of Allegiance

PRESENTATION(S)
 1. NATIONAL HEALTH CENTER WEEK PROCLAMATION
 2. RECOGNITION OF MEDICAL CAMP ORGANIZER
 3. PROCLAMATION TO FORMER MAYOR RICHAR LOYA

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following people provided public comment:
1. Lupita Carranza
2. Maria Consuelo
3. Adela Rivera

STAFF RESPONSE

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION @ 6:42pm

CLOSED SESSION

1.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Consideration of two (2) potential case
 2.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS
  Government Code Section 54957.6
  Agency designated representatives: Ricardo Reyes
  Employee organization: Huntington Park POA

3.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Jon Pina vs. City of Huntington Park, et al.
  Los Angeles County Superior Court Case No. 19STCV23618
  NOT DISCUSSED.

TIME RETURNED 7:56pm

CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT

All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted
by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items prior to the time the
Council votes on the motion unless members of the Council, staff, or the public request
specific items to be discussed and/or removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
action.

  MOTION: Councilmember Martinez moved to approve the Closed Session Item #1
  and Item #2; Item #3 wasn’t discussed. Seconded by Vice Mayor Flores. Motion
  carried by unanimous consent.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Castillo, Sanabria, Martinez, Vice Mayor
  Flores and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  None

  ABSENT:  None

  CONSENT CALENDAR
CITY CLERK

1.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINTUES

  Approve Minute(s) of the following City Council Meeting(s):

  1. Special City Council Meeting held June 4, 2024

  2. Regular City Council Meeting held June 18, 2024

FINANCE

2.  CHECK REGISTER

  RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:
   1. Approve Accounts Payable and Payroll Warrant(s) dated August 5, 2024

3.  FISCAL YEAR 2023 AUDITED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

  RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Receive and file the FY 2023 Audited Financial Statement

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

  4. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL FOR RESIDENT CASE FILE WITH THE
  OWNER-OCCUPIED REHABILITATION PROGRAM FUNDED WITH THE
  CALHOME GRANT IN THE AMOUNT OF $42,951.00 OR UP TO $100,000.

  RECOMMENDED THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to approve payment and to execute related
  documents.

  MOTION: Councilmember Martinez moved to approve the consent calendar,
  seconded by Council member Flores. Motion carried by unanimous consent.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Castillo, Sanabria, Martinez, Vice Mayor
  Flores and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  None

  ABSENT:  None

  END OF CONSENT CALENDAR

  SPECIAL AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL

1.  CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION ADOPTING AND
  AUTHORIZING A MONTHLY AUTOMOBILE ALLOWANCE TO BE PROVIDED TO
  MEMBERS OF THE HUNTINGTON PARK CITY COUNCIL

  MOTION: Vice Mayor Flores moved to approve Resolution adopting and
  authorizing the award of a monthly automobile allowance to members of the
  Huntington Park City Council., second by Councilmember Sanabria. Motion failed
  to obtain majority. Motion did not pass.

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Vice Mayor Flores

  NOES:  Council Member (s): Castillo, Martinez, Mayor Macias

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None
 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

  1. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL TO AWARD PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE ARCHITECTURAL SERVICES AT CITY HALL

  MOTION: Councilmember Martinez moved to Award the professional services
  agreement (PSA) to provide Architectural Services at City Hall to We Architects
  Group for a not-to-exceed fee of $195,060 and Authorize the Finance Director to
  allocate funding into project account number that will pay for this service payable to
  ARPA funds; and Authorize the City manager to execute the professional services
  agreement, seconded by Council member Castillo. Motion carried by unanimous
  consent.

  AYES:  Council Member(s): Castillo, Sanabria, and Martinez, Vice Mayor
  Flores and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  None

  ABSENT:  None

3.  CONSIDERATION OF THE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEE (EDC)
  RECOMMENDED ACTION PERSUANT TO MEASURE PP

  1. MOTION: Councilmember Sanabria moved to Review and discuss the
  recommendations of the Economic Development Committee; and Authorize the
  City Manager to implement the necessary direction of the City Council pursuant to
  the implementation of Measure PP. Seconded by Vice Mayor Flores. Motion
  carried by unanimous consent.

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Martinez, and Castillo Vice Mayor
  Flores and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

4.  DISCUSSION AND/OR ACTION ON THE DISSOLUTION OF THE ECONOMIC
  DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEE

  1. MOTION:

  AYES:  Council Member (s):

  NOES:  None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

  5. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL TO AWARD PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE FAIR HOUSING SERVICES
   MOTION: Vice Mayor Flores moved to Award a One (1) year professional service
  agreement (PSA) to provide fair housing services to the sole responsive and
  responsible proposer, Fair Housing Foundation for a not-to-exceed amount of
  $20,000; and Authorize the City Manager to execute the PSA. Seconded by
  Councilmember Castillo. Motion carried by unanimous consent

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Martinez, and Castillo Vice Mayor
  Flores and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

6. CONSIDERATION AND ADOPTION TO AWARD PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE HOMELESS OUTREACH SERVICES

  MOTION: Councilmember Martinez moved to Award a One (1) year professional
  service agreement (PSA) to provide homeless outreach services to Inner City
  Visions (ICV) for a not-to-exceed amount of $127,330; and Authorize the City
  Manager to execute the PSA. Second by Macias. Motion carried by unanimous
  consent

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Castillo, and Martinez, Vice
  Mayor Flores, and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  Council Member (s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

7. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL TO SOLICIT PROPOSALS FOR FEDERAL
  GRANT COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT ADMINISTRATIVE
  SERVICES

  MOTION: Vice Mayor Flores moved to Authorize staff to publish a Request
  for Proposal (RFP) from qualified community development firms to provide
  professional management and administrative services related to the
  implementation of the City’s Community Development Block Grant (CDBG),
  and other programs funded through the U.S. Department of Housing (HUD)
  and Urban Development and California Department of Housing and
  Community Development (HCD). Second by Macias. Motion carried by
  unanimous consent.

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Castillo, and Martinez, Vice
  Mayor Flores, and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  Council Member (s): None
   ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

PUBLIC WORKS

  8. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL TO AWARD A CONSTRUCTION
  CONTRACT FOR CIP 2019-14 ATP CYCLE V PROJECT

  MOTION: Councilmember Martinez moved to Award the contract to Palp Inc. DBA
  Excel Paving for the construction of CIP 2019 14 ATP Cycle V Project as the
  lowest responsive, responsible bidder for a not to exceed fee of $2,592,810; and
  approve a 10% construction contingency in the amount of $259,281; Appropriate
  $2,852,091; and t Authorize the City Manager to execute the construction contract
  agreement and all change orders in good faith. Second by Macias. Motion carried
  by unanimous consent.

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Castillo, and Martinez, Vice
  Mayor Flores, and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  Council Member (s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

  9. RESOLUTION TO APPROVE ADOPTING A LIST OF PROJECTS FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2024-25 FUNDED BY SENATE BILL 1 (SB1), THE ROAD REPAIR AND
  ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017

  MOTION: Councilmember Martinez moved to adopt Resolution approving the
  Fiscal Year 2024-25 project list for Senate Bill 1 (SB1), the Road Repair and
  Accountability Act of 2017; and Authorize staff to upload the resolution with the
  list of streets to the California Transportation Commission (CTC) website. Second
  by Councilmember Castillo. Motion carried by unanimous consent.

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Castillo, and Martinez, Vice
  Mayor Flores, and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  Council Member (s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

  10. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF SECOND AMENDMENT TO
  CONTRACT SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR MEDIA TECHNICIAN SERVICES

  MOTION: Vice Mayor Flores moved to Approve second amendment to the
  contract services agreement with Mr. Joel Gordillo for media technician
  services extending the term for another three (3) years. Upon conclusion of
  the term, this agreement must come back to the Council for review and
  approval; and Authorize City Manager to execute agreement. Second by
   Councilmember Martinez. Motion carried by unanimous consent

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Castillo, and Martinez, Vice
  Mayor Flores, and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  Council Member (s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

  11. COUNCIL APPOINTMENTS TO VARIOUS COMMISSIONS

  Councilmember Castillo appointed Estella Lopez to the Youth Commission.
  Councilmember Sanabria appointed Nancy Matie to the Civil Service Commission.
  Councilmember Flores appointed Mario Gomez to the Planning Commission and
  Vanessa Bautista to the Civil Service Commission.

  12. CONSIDERATION OF THE CREATION OF A THEATREAND ARTS
  COMMISSION

  1. MOTION: Vice Mayor Flores moved to Review and discuss the addition of a
  Theatre and Arts Commission. Seconded by Martinez. Motion carried unanimously.

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Castillo, and Martinez, Vice
  Mayor Flores, and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  Council Member (s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

POLICE DEPARTMENT

  13. APPROVE THE PURCHASE OF THREE POLICE DEPARTMENT PATROL
  OPERATIONS DIVISION VEHICLES AND SUPPLEMENTARY EQUIPMENT

  1. 1. MOTION: Vice Mayor Flores moved Authorize the requisition of funds to
  purchase three Police Department Patrol Services Division police patrol
  vehicles from FCA US, LLC (DODGE), specifically Carville Chrysler Dodge
  Jeep Ram in Greeneville, TN; and, Approve an expenditure in the amount not to
  exceed $248,038, and request Finance Director identify grant funding source;
  and Authorize the City Manager to purchase the vehicles and equip them with
  the associated technology and emergency response equipment. Seconded by
  Councilmember Sanabria. Motion carried by unanimous consent.

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Castillo, and Martinez, Vice
  Mayor Flores, and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  Council Member (s): None
   ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

COMMUNICATIONS 7 COMMUNITY RELATIONS

  14. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL TO AWARD PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE PUBLIC INFORMATION OFFICER SERVICES,
  PUBLIC AFFAIRS SUPPORT AND STRATEGIC PLANNING FOR SPECIALIZED
  ACTIVITIES

  1. MOTION: Mayor Macias moved to Approve a Contract back to RFP and
  Extending current member for 6 months while staff determines a solution for a
  permanent PIO position. Second by Councilmember Martinez. Motion carried by
  unanimous consent.

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Castillo, and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  Vice Mayor Flores

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): Martinez

CITY MANAGER

  15. CONSIDERATION OF APPROVAL OF A RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING A
  SPENDING LIMITS POLICY FOR PURCHASING AUTHORITY FOR THE CITY
  MANAGER

  1. 1. MOTION: Councilmember Sanabria moved to Adopt Resolution amending
  Resolution No. 2019-04, Establishing A Spending Limits Policy for Purchasing
  Authority for the City Manager. Macias added Friendly Amendment to Approve
  $50,000 limit remove legal portion, and leave settlement at $100,000. Second by
  Flores. Motion carried by unanimous consent.

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Castillo, Martinez, Vice Mayor
  Flores, and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  None

  ABSENT:  None

  16. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF A RESOLUTION FIXING THE ANNUAL
  PENSION TAX RATE TO PAY THE CITY’S PENSION OBLIGATION BOND
  ANNUAL DEBT SERVICE AND A PORTION OF THE COST OF THE PUBLIC
  EMPLOYEES’ RETIREMENT SYSTEM FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025

  MOTION: Vice Mayor Flores moved to Adopt a Resolution Fixing the Rate of
   Taxes to Pay the Cost of the Public Employees Retirement System for the
  Fiscal Year 2024-2025 and Levying Taxes for Said Retirement System to
  the Fiscal Year Beginning July 1, 2024. Second by Councilmember Martinez

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Castillo, and Martinez, Vice
  Mayor Flores, and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  Council Member (s): None

  ABSENT:  Council Member(s): None

  END OF SPECIAL AGENDA

  PUBLIC HEARING(S)

1. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING
COLLECTION OF DELINQUENT REFUSE CHARGES PURSUANT TO SECTION 6-
2.112 OF THE CITY OF HUNTINGTON PARK’S MUNICIPAL CODE (172.54
REFUSE COLLECTION FEES)

  1. MOTION: Councilmember Sanabria moved to Conduct a public hearing; and
  Take public testimony; and Adopt a Resolution directing the County Assessor to
  include delinquent refuse collection fees as a special assessment to be collected at
  the same time and in the same manner as County taxes (172.54 Refuse Collection
  Fees). Public Hearing opened at 9:41pm and closed at 9:41pm. Second by Vice
  Mayor Flores

  AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Castillo, Martinez, Vice Mayor
  Flores, and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  None

  ABSENT:  None

2. CONSIDERATION AND APPROVAL OF A RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING AND
ORDERING THE LEVY AND COLLECTION OF THE ANNUAL SPECIAL TAX FOR
THE CITY OF HUNTINGTON PARK STREET LIGHTING, PARKS, AND
LANDSCAPING SPECIAL TAX DISTRICT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025

  MOTION: Councilmember Martinez moved to Conduct a public hearing; and Take
  public testimony; and Adopt Resolution establishing and ordering the Levy and
  Collection of the Annual Special Tax for the City of Huntington Park Street Lighting,
  Parks and Landscaping Special Tax District for Fiscal Year 2024-2025.
  Public Hearing opened at 9:44pm and closed at 9:45pm. Second by
  Councilmember Sanabria.
   AYES:  Council Member (s): Sanabria, Castillo, Martinez, Vice Mayor
  Flores, and Mayor Macias

  NOES:  None

  ABSENT:  None

DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS

Police Department reported National Night out the next day Tuesday, August 6th 2024.

Parks and Recreation

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS

None

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS
Council member Castillo thanked staff for their hard work. She also wished Vice Mayor
Flores a happy birthday.

Vice Mayor Flores thanked staff for their hard work and congratulated them on their
accomplishments this fiscal year which is noticed by all the growth and progress that is
being made for the city.

Mayor Macias thanked all the staff and directors for their hard work. She also wished
Vice Mayor Flores a happy birthday and a happy belated Father’s Day to all the fathers
out there.

ADJOURNMENT

Mayor Macias adjourned the meeting at 7:28 p.m. The next City of Huntington Park City
Council meeting will be held on Tuesday July 2, 2024 at 6:00 pm
Respectfully submitted.

Eduardo Sarmiento, City Clerk
